newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares open up, set all-time high.
newsitem.headline: French shares open up, set all-time high.

text.p: French shares firmed at the opening on Wednesday, setting an all-time high on the back of a fresh set of opinion polls showing a comfortable majority for the centre-right government, dealers said.
At 0809 GMT, the blue-chip index was up 1.04 percent at 2747.81. Its previous all-time high, of March 11, 1997, was 2,736.71.
The dollar was also higher in Europe, which supported share prices, dealers said.
Last night, a CSA poll gave 317 seats to the centre-right majority against 215 to the Socialists and allies. This follows a BVA poll giving 303 to the majority and 226 to the Socialists and allies.
Last weekend, a Sofres poll gave a lead to the coalition of 338-370 seats against 162-185 for the opposition.
Jacques Chahine Finance said Monday that if the government parties win, fund managers saw the CAC heading above 3,000. If the Socialists win it could fall to 2,400.
At around 0830 GMT the CAC-40 peaked at 2,753.11 before slipping slightly.
But dealers said a number of factors that could puncture the euphoria.

Large fund inflows were currently fuelling the market as foreign funds are comforted by the opinion polls and are willing to invest as France has been lagging behind other markets. First quarter sales figures have also confirmed the recovery potential of the corporate sector.
But any fresh poll showing a swing back to the Socialists could scare these investors away again, they said.
Volume was 1.44 billion francs of which 1.06 billion in CAC-40 shares.
"All signs are on green, the dollar, the bond market and the polls," a broker said. Wall Street closed lower overnight, however, on profit-taking.
The U.S. April Producer Price Index, due at 1230 GMT, and the Consumer Price Index due on Thursday could stop the French rally, dealers said.
The May 20 Federal Reserve Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting could also change the direction.
Oil shares Elf Aquitaine and Total again topped the volume charts, boosted by firmer oil prices. S&P on Tuesday increased Elf's long-term debt rating to "stable" from "negative".
Elf was up 2.21 percent at 601 francs and Total traded 2.89 percent higher at 534 francs.

Eramet, up 2.77 percent at 304.50 francs, was among the top gainers as experts were set to meet over the New Caledonia mine dispute and a shareholders meeting which would have voted on a new chairman was postponed.
